title: Does a DSS extension of Tsai 1998's Theorem 2 (local-energy-estimates Liouville route) exist in the literature, and if so does it reach the repository's screened DSS object?
dispatched_by: orchestrator, following leg 359's finding that Tsai's Theorem 2 (local-energy route) is stated only for the exact-SS ansatz, never checked for a DSS extension specifically

gate_verdict.label: PARTIAL RESULT
gate_verdict.one_line: Chae-Wolf 2016/2017 (arXiv:1610.09464v2) Theorem 1.3 -- the very theorem Pineau-Vicol's DSS Theorem restates and leg 330 already adjudicated -- IS a Liouville-type rigidity theorem for DSS solutions whose proof terminates by literally invoking Tsai 1998's Theorem 2 (local-energy-estimates route) as its finishing move. But it does NOT extend Tsai's local-energy machinery to a genuinely periodic (fixed lambda>1) DSS profile: it reduces DSS to SS via a compactness/degeneration argument valid only as lambda -> 1, then applies Tsai's Theorem 2 UNCHANGED to the resulting SS limit object. This is a genuinely new mechanistic finding for this repository (no prior leg had read Chae-Wolf's primary text closely enough to see the Tsai-Theorem-2 citation at its finishing step) -- but it changes nothing about the bottom line already banked by leg 330: the screened object's lambda-significantly-larger-than-1 clause means the compactness argument's lambda->1 hypothesis is never met, so this partial DSS extension does not reach the screened object either.

clause_by_clause_finding.what_chae_wolf_theorem_1_3_actually_prov: Verbatim (Chae-Wolf v2 l.93-100 region, pdftotext-extracted): 'Theorem 1.3. [For] every C* > 0 [there] exists lambda* > 1 depending on C* [such that for any] lambda-DSS solution [of] Navier-Stokes equations [with] lambda in (1, lambda*), [that] satisfies |u(x,t)| <= C*/sqrt(-t+|x|), then u = 0.' -- a rigidity theorem for GENUINE DSS solutions (period T = 2 log lambda, lambda>1 fixed), not the SS ansatz.
clause_by_clause_finding.proof_mechanism_traced: Section 3 (l.~440-680 of the pdftotext extraction). Proof by contradiction/compactness: assume a sequence of nontrivial lambda_j-DSS solutions u_j with lambda_j -> 1 as j -> infinity, each satisfying the uniform Type-I bound (so a nontrivial DSS solution exists arbitrarily close to lambda=1 despite the theorem's claim). Extract a weak limit u via Banach-Alaoglu + Calderon-Zygmund pressure estimates. Show, via an explicit epsilon/mu argument built on the discrete-self-similarity relation and Arzela-Ascoli compactness of the vorticity on compact sets away from the origin, that for EVERY mu>1, u_mu - u is a harmonic vector field (curl(u_mu - u)=0, div(u_mu-u)=0) and therefore, by the classical Liouville theorem for harmonic functions, u_mu = u identically. This forces u to be EXACTLY (continuously) self-similar for every scaling factor -- i.e. the DSS ansatz has degenerated into the ordinary SS ansatz in the limit. Verbatim, the paper's own next sentence (l.~669-676 of the extraction): 'u [is] backward self-similar ... In particular, u satisfies local energy estimate (3.4). Thus, [we are] in [a] position to apply Tsai's result [15, Theorem 2], u [is] identical[ly] zero.' This contradicts the uniform-non-triviality lower bound (3.9) established earlier in the same proof, completing the contradiction argument.
clause_by_clause_finding.is_this_a_local_energy_estimates_mechani: NO, not directly -- and this is the precise, load-bearing distinction. The local-energy-estimates step (Tsai's Theorem 2 itself) is invoked UNCHANGED, as a black box, and it is applied to the LIMIT profile u, which the compactness argument has already forced to be genuinely SS (not merely DSS). Nothing in Chae-Wolf's Section 3 re-derives or generalizes Tsai's A_p-weight / CKN-type partial-regularity machinery (Tsai 1998 Section 4) for a profile that is periodic-in-log-time with a FIXED lambda>1 -- i.e. for an object that stays genuinely DSS rather than degenerating to SS. The mechanism that reaches DSS solutions is the compactness/harmonic-Liouville argument (Section 3, novel to Chae-Wolf), NOT an extension of Tsai's local-energy-estimates machinery to the DSS ansatz. Tsai's Theorem 2 is consumed only at the very end, on an object that is, by that point, no longer discretely self-similar in the nontrivial sense.
clause_by_clause_finding.why_this_forces_lambda_near_1_specifical: The compactness argument needs lambda_j -> 1 to force k_j = k(lambda_j, mu) with lambda_j^{k_j} -> mu for EVERY fixed mu>1 (l.~600-660 of the extraction, the k_j construction) -- this is exactly what proves u_mu=u for every mu, i.e. genuine SS in the limit. For a FIXED lambda significantly larger than 1 (the screened object's regime) there is no such sequence lambda_j -> 1 to run compactness over, and the degenerate-to-SS argument has no analogue: the mechanism is structurally incapable of reaching fixed-large-lambda DSS objects, not merely failing there by a slack constant.

classification_against_tsai_theorem_2s_f.what_it_covers: Liouville-type rigidity for genuinely DSS (period-T, lambda fixed) weak solutions satisfying the SAME Type-I decay bound (1.3)/(1.4) that appears in Tsai's motivating example -- but ONLY for lambda in an unspecified-but-nonempty interval (1, lambda*(C_that_0)) forced arbitrarily close to 1 by the proof's own compactness step. This is a genuine widening of Tsai's reach from the SS ansatz to a strict superset (DSS solutions with lambda near 1), and it is the closest thing in the literature to a 'DSS extension' of Tsai's Theorem 2 route -- because it terminates in an unmodified application of Tsai's Theorem 2 itself.
classification_against_tsai_theorem_2s_f.what_it_does_not_cover: It does not cover DSS solutions with lambda bounded away from 1 (no version of the argument works for a fixed large lambda -- the compactness step has no lambda_j -> 1 sequence to exploit). It does not generalize Tsai's LOCAL-ENERGY-ESTIMATES MACHINERY itself (Tsai Section 4, the A_p-weight/CKN partial-regularity argument that establishes the sub-linear growth bound) to a periodic-in-s profile; that machinery is used only on the emergent SS limit. So relative to the dispatch's exact ask -- 'a theorem that proves Liouville-type rigidity for DSS ... weak solutions using a local-energy-estimates mechanism analogous to Tsai's, or that explicitly extends/generalizes Tsai's Theorem 2 to the DSS ansatz' -- Chae-Wolf's Theorem 1.3 satisfies the FIRST disjunct (DSS rigidity via a route that uses Tsai's local-energy mechanism as its finishing step) but NOT the second (it does not generalize Theorem 2's proof to the DSS ansatz; it reduces DSS to SS first and applies Theorem 2 unchanged).

reach_against_the_screened_object.verdict: DOES NOT REACH -- same bottom line leg 330 already banked, now explained mechanistically
reach_against_the_screened_object.deciding_clause: screened object's lambda is 'significantly larger than 1' (leg 251/leg 260/leg 313's structural specification, an OUTPUT of the search, no number to clear); Chae-Wolf's Theorem 1.3 (= PV's DSS theorem, already quoted verbatim by leg 330: 'There exists lambda-bar = lambda-bar(C_{U,0}) > 1, such that if 1 < lambda < lambda-bar, then U = 0') only reaches lambda in a window forced near 1 by the compactness argument's own construction
reach_against_the_screened_object.cross_check_against_leg_330: leg 330's clause-by-clause ledger (H1-H6 in writeup/novelty/leg_330.md and experiments/journal/leg_330.md section 4) is reused here without modification -- it is the identical theorem under PV's restatement -- the deciding clause H5 (the lambda-near-1 window) stands unchanged. This leg's contribution is NOT a re-adjudication of the reach question (already settled) but an identification of WHY the theorem's reach is structurally confined to lambda near 1: the mechanism is a compactness-forced degeneration to the SS ansatz, not a DSS-native local-energy argument, so there was never a route by which it could have reached fixed-large-lambda DSS objects, independent of how tightly the non-explicit constant lambda*(C_{U,0}) could in principle be bounded.
